concern.concern: Proof 5.1 concludes that each field evaluation is measurable with respect to the completion of G=σ(Y(e_n):n), and hence that the full field sigma-algebra is contained in that completion. Almost-sure equality with a G-measurable variable only gives this for the ambient augmentation by all ambient null events; it need not give membership in the ordinary completion of G. For example, take X=H=R, K=0, ε=1, an independent standard-normal prior U, standard-normal ξ and an independent Bernoulli(0) coordinate with event N={coordinate=1}. Set Z(g)=gξ except Z(2)=2ξ+1_N. This satisfies the stated Gaussian and L2-linearity assumptions. With supplied basis {1}, G=σ(ξ), while the full field reveals N through Y(2)−2Y(1). N is not contained in any G-measurable null set. The theorem's independence conclusion remains accessible directly from the already established independence with every finite observation block and a generating-cylinder argument, but the written completion inclusion needs qualification.
